title: Isolated Flat Points and $C^2$-Robustness of the No Focal Points Property
summary: We prove a local stability criterion for the no focal points property on compact Riemannian surfaces. More precisely, if a smooth metric $g$ has non-positive Gaussian curvature and its zero-curvature set is finite, then $g$ belongs to the $C^2$-interior of the set of metrics without focal points. Thus, every sufficiently small $C^2$-perturbation of $g$ still has no focal points, although arbitrarily small perturbations may create regions of positive Gaussian curvature.
